+//! Provenance: the public values of sketch chaining - options, identities, chains, rejections
+//! and the named errors. Our own design for issue 1861; no vendor material consulted.
+
+use crate::dxf::Primitive;
+use crate::geo2d::Point2;
+use std::fmt;
+
+/// Default join tolerance in millimetres.
+pub const DEFAULT_JOIN_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.01;
+/// The smallest join tolerance: above the identity quantum (1e-6 mm), so two joints of one
+/// chain never share a quantized position.
+pub const MIN_JOIN_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-5;
+/// The largest join tolerance, in millimetres.
+pub const MAX_JOIN_TOLERANCE: f64 = 10.0;
+/// Input size limit; above it the call is refused.
+pub const MAX_PRIMITIVES: usize = 2_000_000;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, thiserror::Error)]
+pub enum ChainError {
+    #[error("sketch chaining: join tolerance must be between 1e-5 mm and 10 mm")]
+    InvalidTolerance,
+    #[error("sketch chaining: primitive {primitive} has a non-finite value")]
+    NonFinite { primitive: usize },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: primitive {primitive} lies outside the supported coordinate range")]
+    OutOfRange { primitive: usize },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: primitive {primitive} is invalid: {reason}")]
+    InvalidPrimitive {
+        primitive: usize,
+        reason: &'static str,
+    },
+    #[error(
+        "sketch chaining: the drawing is too large or too dense to chain within the work limit"
+    )]
+    TooComplex,
+    #[error("sketch chaining: primitive {primitive} repeats primitive {of} on the same layer")]
+    DuplicatePrimitive { primitive: usize, of: usize },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: primitive {primitive} is shorter than the join tolerance")]
+    DegenerateSegment { primitive: usize },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: {degree} curve ends meet at ({}, {}); a chain cannot branch", at.x, at.y)]
+    Branch { at: Point2, degree: usize },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: closed loop crosses or touches itself at ({}, {})", at.x, at.y)]
+    SelfCrossing { at: Point2 },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: closed loop encloses no area")]
+    ZeroArea,
+    #[error("sketch chaining: chain repeats chain {of}")]
+    DuplicateChain { of: ChainId },
+    #[error("sketch chaining: nesting is ambiguous: chain {other} crosses or touches a loop at ({}, {})", at.x, at.y)]
+    NestingAmbiguous { other: ChainId, at: Point2 },
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct ChainOptions {
+    /// Ends closer than this (mm) are joined; a wider gap is never bridged.
+    pub join_tolerance: f64,
+}
+
+impl Default for ChainOptions {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        ChainOptions {
+            join_tolerance: DEFAULT_JOIN_TOLERANCE,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Identity of a chain: a hash of its layer name and its quantized curves in canonical order.
+/// It does not depend on the order or direction the primitives were drawn in.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
+pub struct ChainId(pub u128);
+
+impl fmt::Display for ChainId {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
+        write!(f, "{:032x}", self.0)
+    }
+}
+
+/// One input primitive in walk direction.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct ChainSegment {
+    /// Index of the primitive in the input slice.
+    pub primitive: usize,
+    /// The analytic curve, turned to the walk direction (an arc keeps centre and radius; its
+    /// sweep sign says clockwise or counterclockwise).
+    pub curve: Primitive,
+    /// The walk runs against the drawn direction.
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub start: Point2,
+    pub end: Point2,
+}
+
+/// A chain with two free ends. It starts at its lower end in (x, y).
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct OpenChain {
+    pub id: ChainId,
+    pub layer: String,
+    pub segments: Vec<ChainSegment>,
+    pub start: Point2,
+    pub end: Point2,
+    /// The widest joint gap inside the chain, at most the join tolerance.
+    pub max_gap: f64,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum LoopRole {
+    /// Inside an even number of other loops: material lies inside it.
+    Outer,
+    /// Inside an odd number of other loops: a hole in its parent.
+    Hole,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct Nesting {
+    pub role: LoopRole,
+    /// How many closed chains contain this one.
+    pub depth: usize,
+    /// The innermost chain that contains this one.
+    pub parent: Option<ChainId>,
+}
+
+/// A closed loop, walked counterclockwise from its lowest joint in (x, y).
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct ClosedChain {
+    pub id: ChainId,
+    pub layer: String,
+    pub segments: Vec<ChainSegment>,
+    /// Enclosed area in mm^2, arcs included exactly.
+    pub area: f64,
+    /// The widest joint gap inside the loop, at most the join tolerance.
+    pub max_gap: f64,
+    /// Outer boundary or hole; `NestingAmbiguous` when this loop or one around it crosses or
+    /// touches another closed chain, so no reading is safe.
+    pub nesting: Result<Nesting, ChainError>,
+}
+
+/// Primitives that form no usable chain, and why.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct Rejected {
+    pub layer: String,
+    /// Input indices, ascending.
+    pub primitives: Vec<usize>,
+    pub error: ChainError,
+}
+
+/// Every chain of the input, each list sorted by layer name, then start position, then id.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
+pub struct SketchChains {
+    pub closed: Vec<ClosedChain>,
+    pub open: Vec<OpenChain>,
+    pub rejected: Vec<Rejected>,
+}
+
+impl SketchChains {
+    /// The chains, or the first rejection or ambiguous nesting as an error.
+    pub fn strict(self) -> Result<SketchChains, ChainError> {
+        if let Some(rejected) = self.rejected.first() {
+            return Err(rejected.error.clone());
+        }
+        if let Some(error) = self
+            .closed
+            .iter()
+            .find_map(|chain| chain.nesting.as_ref().err())
+        {
+            return Err(error.clone());
+        }
+        Ok(self)
+    }
+}

+## #1861 - Sketch chaining, outer-versus-hole nesting and open-chain safety
+
+**What was decided.** Add `camcraft-geometry::sketch_chains`: one call,
+`chain(&[LayeredPrimitive], ChainOptions) -> Result<SketchChains, ChainError>`,
+that turns the DXF reader's lines, arcs and circles (#1860) into closed loops
+and open chains. No new dependency, no file I/O, no application state.
+Primitives and the join tolerance are in millimetres; the caller scales a
+document by its units first.
+
+- **Joining.** Curve ends within the join tolerance (default 0.01 mm, allowed
+  1e-5 mm to 10 mm) are clustered with a uniform grid and union-find. Ends
+  join only on the same layer, because the layer name is part of a chain's
+  identity. A gap wider than the tolerance is never bridged: the chain stays
+  open and reports both free ends. A bridged gap is reported as `max_gap`.
+- **Curves stay analytic.** A chain segment is the input primitive turned to
+  the walk direction (`reversed`, with the arc's start angle and sweep sign
+  rewritten). Nothing is flattened, snapped or healed, so a later operation
+  can still post G2/G3 from centre, radius and sweep sign.
+- **Canonical order.** A closed loop is walked counterclockwise (by its exact
+  signed area, arcs included) from its lowest joint in (x, y). An open chain
+  starts at its lower end. The result does not depend on the order or the
+  direction the primitives were drawn in.
+- **`ChainId`.** The 128-bit FNV-1a hash of a version tag, the layer name, the
+  closed flag and the curves in canonical order, each quantized to 1e-6 mm.
+  The minimum tolerance is above that quantum, so two joints of one chain
+  never share a quantized position and the canonical start is unique. The
+  value for a reference slot is pinned in a test, and checked there against a
+  DXF polyline of the same shape, because a project file may store it (#1862).
+- **Refusals are per chain and named.** `Err` is only for input nothing can be
+  read from: a bad tolerance, a non-finite, out-of-range or invalid primitive,
+  or a drawing over the limits. Everything else comes back in the result:
+  `closed`, `open`, and `rejected` (layer, input indices, `ChainError`):
+  `DuplicatePrimitive`, `DegenerateSegment`, `Branch`, `SelfCrossing`,
+  `ZeroArea`, `DuplicateChain`. `SketchChains::strict()` turns the first
+  rejection or ambiguous nesting into an `Err` for callers that want all or
+  nothing. Every input primitive ends in exactly one chain or one rejection.
+- **Branches are a diagnostic, not a traversal.** Three or more ends at one
+  joint reject the whole connected component with `Branch { at, degree }`.
+- **Self-crossing.** A closed loop is tested exactly, line against arc against
+  circle in closed form, over a watertight copy whose joint gaps carry straight
+  bridges. Contact within the tolerance of a joint between the two elements
+  that meet there is the joint itself; any other contact, touching included,
+  is `SelfCrossing { at }`.
+- **Nesting.** Depth is counted by an exact crossing-number test against the
+  arcs themselves. Even depth is `Outer`, odd is `Hole`, with the innermost
+  container as `parent`: the even-odd rule of `geo2d::Region`. Nesting is read
+  over every closed chain passed in, across layers; a caller that wants the
+  nesting of one layer passes only that layer's primitives.
+- **Crossing loops get no reading.** Two closed chains that cross or touch
+  keep their geometry and identity, but their `nesting` is
+  `Err(NestingAmbiguous)`, and so is that of every loop inside one of them.
+- **Limits.** Coordinates below 1e7 mm, at most 2,000,000 primitives, and a
+  budget of 200,000,000 pair tests per call. Over the budget the call returns
+  `TooComplex`; it does not hang.
+
+**Why.** A wrong outer-or-hole reading puts the cutter on the wrong side of a
+contour, so every doubtful case is refused or left without a reading instead
+of guessed. Partial results follow the Prime Directive's "prefer recoverable
+states": a stray scribble on one layer must not block the import of a clean
+part on another, and the rejection says which primitives and why.
+
+**Sources.** Fixed-radius neighbour search on a grid (Bentley, Stanat and
+Williams 1977); union-find (Tarjan 1975); FNV-1a (IETF draft-eastlake-fnv);
+sweep and prune with the widest-spread axis (Cohen, Lin, Manocha and Ponamgi
+1995; Ericson 2005); segment, line-circle and circle-circle contacts (O'Rourke
+1998; Schneider and Eberly 2003); crossing-number containment (Shimrat 1962;
+Haines 1994); area by Green's theorem. Each submodule names its own. No vendor
+code, file or output was consulted.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- *Reuse `boundary_chains::group_runs`.* It joins point lists in pick order on
+  fixed quantized keys; it has no caller tolerance and no curve metadata (the
+  earlier attempt's finding on the issue).
+- *Nest with `geo2d::Region` / Clipper directly.* `Region::new` unions and
+  renormalizes its loops, so a result loop cannot be traced back to a
+  `ChainId`, and it needs flattened arcs, where chord error can flip a
+  near-tangent containment. The exact test uses the same even-odd rule; a
+  test compares its reading with `Region` over flattened copies.
+- *Deterministic traversal through a branch* (leftmost turn). It would pick
+  one of several loops for the user without saying so.
+- *Snap joined ends together.* It would move arc ends off their circles and
+  change centre or radius.
+- *`std` hashing for the id.* Its output is not stable across Rust releases.
+- *One global error for any bad chain.* See "Why".
+- *A plain x sweep for the crossing search.* A tall outline with finely
+  divided vertical sides kept every side open at once and ran into the budget
+  (pinned by a test).
+
+**Known limits.**
+- Two curves that meet at a tangent cusp (the path turns back on itself along
+  a shared tangent) can read as `SelfCrossing` when coordinate rounding makes
+  them cross a little way from the joint. Tangent continuations (fillets,
+  S-curves) are not affected and are pinned by a test.
+- Open chains are not tested for self-crossing: an engraved script letter may
+  cross itself.
+- There is no flattening helper; the operations that need polygons (#1867)
+  choose their own chord tolerance.
+
+**Cost to change later.** The id recipe is the expensive part: changing the
+quantum, the canonical order or the fed bytes changes every stored `ChainId`.
+The version tag in the hash (`camcraft-sketch-chain-v1`) exists so that such a
+change is a new, non-aliasing id space. Everything else is internal to the
+module.

+## #1862 - A DXF profile on the stock of a setup, and the virtual model reference
+
+The maintainer's words (issue 1862, 2026-11-15): "A DXF should be possible to
+"place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a
+model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just
+make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly.
+The Adding DXF Profile, should thus live on "Stock page" and have a "virtual"
+model reference, just so the operations pages gets happy about a model being
+loaded.."
+
+### What a profile is in the ECS
+
+- **A `Sketch` component on a named entity** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`),
+  beside `Name` and `Location`. It holds `setup: Option<String>` (the
+  declared-vs-effective law of `Operation::setup`) and `data:
+  Arc<SketchData>`. The entity never has `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is
+  false for it, so the part readers (`model::model_entities`) and each 3D
+  solid tool do not see it.
+- **`SketchData` is in `camcraft-geometry`** (`sketch_data`), not in `app`:
+  it works only on domain values. It holds the primitives in millimetres, the
+  layer names, the source units (the file's `$INSUNITS` and the unit applied),
+  the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. Its
+  fields are private and the two constructors make the chains, so the stored
+  chains are always the chains of the stored primitives.
+- **The `Location` of a profile is relative to the stock**, as the scope
+  change says: the frame is the top face of the stock of the setup, at the
+  stock origin, turned with the stock (`sketch::face_frame`). The stock origin
+  is the origin of the stock entity (for a box and a cylinder: the centre in
+  XY). The top is the box height, the cylinder height, or the highest facet Z
+  of a stock made from a model. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face
+  normal only. Because the placement is relative, a moved or resized stock
+  carries the profile, and nothing must follow it by a second command. The
+  stock is setup furniture, so a setup's part alignment does not move the
+  profile.
+- **Deleting the entity frees the drawing.** The component is a Rust-owned
+  type; the last `Arc` holder drops the data
+  (`deleting_the_entity_frees_its_drawing`).
+
+### The commands
+
+- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** reads, checks and chains
+  the file at construction. `setup` is the new argument (`None`: the active
+  setup). A setup without a stock is refused ("make a stock first"). A file
+  with no unit and no unit from the caller is the typed
+  `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing`; it has the drawing extents, so the UI of
+  issue 1863 can show them in each unit before it asks. A unit from the caller
+  wins over the unit of the file (the argument is an override).
+- **`MoveSketch` moves a profile; `MoveModel` refuses one by name.** The issue
+  body said `MoveModel`. That was written before the scope change. `MoveModel`
+  writes a world placement and carries the stock; a profile has a face
+  placement (X, Y, angle) and rides the stock. Two verbs on one object would
+  split the undo story (the "pages own their verbs" law of `MoveModel`), so
+  the profile has its own command and the placement cannot leave the face.
+  Dropped: a `MoveModel` that accepts a profile and silently drops Z and tilt.
+- **A name from the file stem is made unique** (`plate`, `plate (2)`), so one
+  drawing can be placed more than one time on a sheet. A stated name that is
+  in use is refused.
+- **`DeleteSetup` refuses a setup with a placed profile** (as it refuses one
+  with operations). Dropped: deleting the profiles with the setup, which loses
+  work without a word.
+- The Z of the drawing (`Document::elevation`) is not used: the profile lies
+  on the stock face.
+
+### What the virtual model reference is
+
+- **It is derived, not stored**: `sketch_model::of(world, setup)` is `Some`
+  when the setup has one or more placed profiles and the document has no part
+  (a model that is not a fixture). No component and no file key holds it, so
+  it cannot disagree with the document. Dropped: a tag component or a
+  placeholder model entity. A placeholder entity must be kept in step by each
+  command that adds or removes a model or a profile, and a facet-less "model"
+  in `model_entities` is the zero-triangle mesh that the issue forbids.
+- **It has no facets.** It names profiles only.
+- **An operation refers to a profile as `SrcRef::Entity(<profile name>)`.**
+
+### Which checks read it
+
+| Check | Reads | Result on a virtual reference |
+|---|---|---|
+| The source door of each operation command (`gates::valid_src`, `sketch_gate`: create, paste, retarget, retype, move to a setup) | `sketch_model::source_problem` | A profile is a source for the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections, in its own setup. Each other kind refuses: "needs a solid model - '<name>' is a DXF profile, a virtual model reference with no solid". |
+| The same door, 3D milling and multi-axis sections, each source | `sketch_model::of` | Refused: "a <kind> operation needs a solid model - the setup has only its stock and the DXF profile ..." |
+| The model-height diagnostic (`operation::missing_source`, Top/Bottom of Model) | `sketch_model::of` | The text names the virtual reference and says to use a stock or fixed height. It is not "no model loaded". The height has no value: a reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. |
+| The generation door (`operation::collect_job`) | `sketch_model::generation_problem` | Refused by name with what the operation is checked against (the stock and the chains). |
+| `get_job` (MCP) | `sketch_model::of`, `checked_against` | Each setup has `model_reference` (`solid`, `virtual` with its profiles, or null); an operation on a profile has `checks_against`. |
+| The operation pages (issue 1863) | `sketch_model::model_loaded` | True for a part or a virtual reference. |
+
+Checks that need a solid part keep their refusal: part alignment and locate
+("import a model first"), fit stock to models, the WCS box points of a model,
+mesh repair, fixture tags, stock from a model.
+
+### Why nothing passes silently
+
+This PR does not make a toolpath from profile chains: that is issue 1864
+(chain picks, side and direction per chain, stock and crossing checks without
+a mesh). Until then generation of an operation on a profile is refused by name,
+so no gouge, collision or verify check can pass because the model is virtual.
+The operation has no toolpath, and the post gate refuses it.
+
+### What the project file stores
+
+- A profile is an entity row with `kind: "sketch"`. Its `translation` and
+  `rotation` are the face placement. Its `sketch` key has: `setup`, `insunits`
+  (the code the file stated, 0 for none), `unit` (the `$INSUNITS` code of the
+  unit applied), `join_tolerance`, `layers`, `primitives` (mm, radians; each
+  names its layer by index), and the import counts (`entities`, `vertices`,
+  `skipped`).
+- **The chains are not stored.** They are made again from the primitives at
+  load, by the same `chain()` call as at import. Dropped: storing the chains.
+  A stored chain can disagree with its primitives after a hand edit, and the
+  chain identities of issue 1861 do not depend on the order of the input.
+- **The virtual model reference is not stored.**
+- Each profile is read and chained before any world write. A profile off its
+  face, with an unknown unit code or with primitives that do not chain refuses
+  the file by name.
+- **`PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63.** A v62 file has no profile row and steps up
+  unchanged. An old reader refuses a v63 file. (A v62 reader also refuses the
+  kind word `sketch`; the version gives the clear message.) PR #2077 and PR
+  #2126 also take v63 at this time. The PR that merges second takes the next
+  number when it merges main.
+
+### What it costs to change later
+
+- A stored reference or stored chains need a new project version and a
+  migration.
+- If Top/Bottom of Model must have a value on a virtual reference (for
+  example the stock top and the stock bottom), `operation::resolve_height`
+  gets one arm; operations saved before that keep the refusal until then.
+- A profile on a different stock face (a side, the bottom) needs a face
+  choice on `Sketch` and in the file.
+
+### PR #2134 review fixes
+
+- **Reserve the stock source word without regard to letter case.** Explicit
+  profile names such as `stock` and `STOCK` are refused. The same file stems
+  use the existing `profile` fallback and unique-name handling. The MCP
+  source reader treats these words as stock, so accepting them as profile
+  names could silently select different geometry. Dropped: accepting
+  ambiguous aliases or changing the source-reference format for this fix.
+  An unambiguous source-reference format later needs coordinated changes to
+  the source reader and its callers.
+- **Validate summary counts in both `SketchData` constructors.** Entity and
+  vertex counts must fit the default DXF import limits. The skipped counts
+  are added with checked arithmetic, and their total must fit the entity
+  limit. This check runs before the empty-drawing refusal. The validated
+  total is retained for `profile_view`, so it never adds untrusted counts.
+  Invalid stored summaries become the existing project error naming the
+  profile before any world write. Dropped: unchecked addition, a panic, or
+  saturating addition that hides invalid saved data. Changing these limits
+  later requires changing the constructor validation and its pins; no new
+  project field or version is needed for the derived total.
